analysis.investment_thesis: IGL is a textbook regulated utility monopoly — it owns the only CNG and piped gas network in Delhi/NCR, making it the toll road of natural gas distribution. At 14.2x earnings with virtually zero debt and consistent 15%+ net profit CAGR over nine years, the price is fair for the quality on offer.
key_strengths: Geographic monopoly: pipeline infrastructure creates an insurmountable natural moat — no competitor can economically duplicate the network
Fortress balance sheet: debt/equity of 0.01, equity grew from INR 5,358 Cr to INR 11,221 Cr in five years, and OCF positive all 5 years
Durable regulatory moat: city gas distribution licenses grant exclusive rights for 25 years, providing predictable, inflation-linked pricing power
key_risks: FY2025 net profit fell to INR 1,713 Cr from INR 1,983 Cr in FY2024 — margin compression from gas procurement cost volatility is real
Regulatory pricing risk: government intervention in CNG prices could compress spread between APM gas cost and retail tariff
EV adoption threatens long-term CNG vehicle volumes, the highest-margin segment
red_flags: Operating income declined to INR 1,994 Cr in FY2025 from INR 2,388 Cr in FY2024 — consecutive-year profit decline warrants monitoring
Heavy capex (INR 1,100–1,300 Cr annually) keeps free cash flow modest relative to earnings, limiting near-term capital return
analysis.detailed_analysis:
IGL is the kind of business I understand and love — it distributes a utility under a government-granted monopoly, has pricing power built into its regulatory framework, and runs on almost no debt while generating consistent cash. The nine-year net profit CAGR of 15.8% and ROCE of 20.8% confirm this is a high-quality compounder. The only real blemish is the FY2025 earnings dip, driven by gas procurement cost spikes that temporarily squeezed the margin between APM allocation price and retail CNG tariffs — a cyclical, not structural, issue.

At a forward P/E of 12.4x and EV/EBITDA of 10.2x, the market is not pricing in the durability of this monopoly franchise. Persistent FII (17%) and DII (23%) institutional ownership signals sophisticated long-term holders. The expanding CWIP (INR 1,701 Cr) suggests geographic expansion into new areas, which will underpin the next leg of volume growth. This is a fair price for a wonderful regulated business.
